Recreation Services
The Recreation Division of the Parks and Recreation Department is comprised of four sections: Community Services; Sports, Aquatics, and Camps; Cultural, and Social Services. The Community Services section conducts recreation and neighborhood center programs at various City parks and school facilities. A variety of recreation programs in the following categories are conducted at 184 sites:
Neighborhood Park and Elementary School Program:
Activities include sports, Saturday leagues, games, clubs, crafts, special events, parties and play days.
Junior and Senior High School Program:
Activities include supervised sports, clinics, clubs, trips, dances, and dropin centers where various table games are available.
Neighborhood Center Program:
Activities are tailored to the particular needs of the community surrounding the center and may include classes, clubs, work shops, contests, festivals, performing groups, and volunteer opportunity information and referrals.
Community Centers, Neighborhood Centers, and Other Special Facilities:
Community centers provide a setting for programmed social, educational, and cultural activities. A community center provides meeting room, classroom, and specialized equipment room facilities. San Jose currently provides three community centers: St. James, Leininger, and South Side. Each contains approximately 10,000 square feet of building space.
A total of eighteen neighborhood centers are provided, nine of which are located on City park sites, nine on school sites. These centers generally contain 1,500 to 2,000 square feet. Organized programming is conducted on a limited basis as appropriate for resident needs within each neighborhood.
Included in other City special facilities are the Community Theater, the Civic Auditorium, various facilities located in Kelly Park, the Police Activities League Sports Center, Municipal S dium, and others.
